flow: Susceptible Adult Female Vectors->Exposed Adult Female Vectors
Exposed Adult Female Vectors->Infectious Adult Female Vectors
param: b Average biting rate per unit time of a female mosquito (paper: typically 0.3 to 0.5 per day).
β Percentage/probability that a bite transmits ZIKV (paper Table 1: 0.05–0.12).
M Amount/number of alternative hosts besides human in the environment (affects bites received by humans via (N_H+M)).
λ Human population growth rate used in logistic growth term (Table 2).
K_H Human carrying capacity for logistic growth (Table 2; Rio example).
α_H Inverse incubation time (progression rate) of ZIKV in humans (Table 1: incubation time 2–4 days).
γ Human recovery rate (inverse of recovery time; Table 1: recovery time 5–7 days).
e Number of eggs laid per female mosquito per unit time (Table 1: 80 per day).
τ1 Egg development rate (reciprocal of egg development time; Table 1: 3 days).
μ1 Egg mortality rate (Table 1).
τ2 Larval development rate (reciprocal of larval development time; Table 1: 9 days).
μ2 Larval mortality rate (Table 1).
τ3 Pupal development rate (reciprocal of pupal development time; Table 1: 3 days).
μ3 Pupal mortality rate (Table 1).
μ_V Adult vector mortality rate (Table 1).
q Percentage of females among adult vectors (Table 1).
κ Larvae mortality rate due to limited carrying capacity (logistic term in larvae equation; Table 2).
K_V Carrying capacity for larvae (vector aquatic stage) (Table 2; Rio example).
α_V Inverse incubation time (progression rate) of ZIKV in vectors (Table 1: incubation time 8–12 days; Table 2 uses 10 days).
c_H Composite factor in human force of infection: (β b I_V)/(N_H+M). (Paper: exposure rate of a human).
c_V Composite factor in mosquito force of infection: (β b I_H)/(N_H+M). (Paper: exposure rate of a mosquito).
